answer: Sybil resistance here uses quadratic stake: an agent's voting weight is the square root of the tokens it locks, so splitting a hoard across many fake identities shrinks influence instead of multiplying it. One honest agent with an anchor stake of 100 votes at 10; an attacker wanting that same 10 must lock 100 per fake identity, and two Sybils need 400. A one-time opal deposit is slashed on detected fraud, while a shale registration fee burns on every new identity. To mimic ten honest agents the attacker locks a hundred times the capital, making the attack cost far exceed any reward.
